newsitem.title: GERMANY: Ruhrgas buys stake in Sweden's Vattenfall Naturgas.
newsitem.headline: Ruhrgas buys stake in Sweden's Vattenfall Naturgas.

text.p: German gas company Ruhrgas AG said on Wednesday that it bought 14.5 percent of Swedish gas company Vattenfall Naturgas AB.
Burckhard Bergmann, deputy head of Ruhrgas, said in a statement that the Vattenfall stake would give the German firm a chance to participate in the growing Swedish gas industry.
The Swedish power company Vattenfall Stromkonzern AB, the parent of Vattenfall Naturgas, is also selling 14.5 percent of the gas company to Norway's Statoil, Ruhrgas added.
Finnish oil and energy group Neste Oy and Danish firm Dansk Olje og Naturgas A/S will each purchase a 10 percent stake in Vattenfall Naturgas.
Vattenfall Naturgas is expected to sell nearly 900 million cubic metres of natural gas this year, up from slightly more than 850 million in 1996, with turnover at around 850 million Swedish crowns.
Vattenfall brings natural gas through its own pipeline to Gothenburg in south-west Sweden from Dragor in Denmark. It then sells the gas to 55,000 end-users in south-west Sweden.
The Vattenfall pipeline is part of the Nordic Gas Grid, which is on the list of the European Union's Trans-European Energy Network (TEN).
Earlier this month, Ruhrgas signed a transit contract with Belgium's natural gas distributor Distrigas/Distrigaz to transport British gas to the German border via the Belgian port of Zeebrugge.
Ruhrgas also signed a deal with Britain's British Petroleum Co Plc (BP) earlier this month. Under the deal, BP will supply gas to Ruhrgas from its British offshore fields from next year.
Ruhrgas has also been involved in trying to buy a 30 percent stake with Preussen and Russia's Gazprom in the Latvian state gas company, Latvian Gas.
